elements.short: The definition of a specific activity to be taken, independent of any particular patient or context
elements.definition: This resource allows for the definition of some activity to be performed, independent of a particular patient, practitioner, or other performance context.

elements.short: Metadata about the resource
elements.definition: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

elements.short: A set of rules under which this content was created
elements.definition: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.

elements.short: Language of the resource content
elements.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.

elements.short: Text summary of the resource, for human interpretation
elements.definition: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

elements.short: Canonical identifier for this activity definition, represented as a URI (globally unique)

This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which at which an authoritative instance of this activity definition is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the activity definition is stored on different servers.

elements.short: Additional identifier for the activity definition
elements.definition: A formal identifier that is used to identify this activity definition when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.

elements.short: Business version of the activity definition
elements.definition: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the activity definition when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the activity definition author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence. To provide a version consistent with the Decision Support Service specification, use the format Major.Minor.Revision (e.g. 1.0.0). For more information on versioning knowledge assets, refer to the Decision Support Service specification. Note that a version is required for non-experimental active assets.

elements.short: Name for this activity definition (computer friendly)
elements.definition: A natural language name identifying the activity definition. This name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation.

elements.short: Name for this activity definition (human friendly)
elements.definition: A short, descriptive, user-friendly title for the activity definition.

elements.short: Subordinate title of the activity definition
elements.definition: An explanatory or alternate title for the activity definition giving additional information about its content.

elements.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired {{title}} without due consideration
elements.short: draft | active | retired | unknown
elements.definition: The status of this activity definition. Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content.

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

elements.short: For testing purposes, not real usage
elements.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this activity definition is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and is not intended to be used for genuine usage.

elements.short: Type of individual the activity definition is intended for
elements.definition: A code or group definition that describes the intended subject of the activity being defined.

binding.description: The possible types of subjects for an activity (E.g. Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, etc.).

elements.short: Date last changed
elements.definition: The date  (and optionally time) when the activity definition was published. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the activity definition changes.

elements.short: Name of the publisher (organization or individual)
elements.definition: The name of the organization or individual that published the activity definition.

elements.short: Contact details for the publisher
elements.definition: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.

elements.short: Natural language description of the activity definition
elements.definition: A free text natural language description of the activity definition from a consumer's perspective.

elements.short: The context that the content is intended to support
elements.definition: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate activity definition instances.

elements.short: Intended jurisdiction for activity definition (if applicable)
elements.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the activity definition is intended to be used.

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

elements.short: Why this activity definition is defined
elements.definition: Explanation of why this activity definition is needed and why it has been designed as it has.

elements.short: Describes the clinical usage of the activity definition
elements.definition: A detailed description of how the activity definition is used from a clinical perspective.

elements.short: Use and/or publishing restrictions
elements.definition: A copyright statement relating to the activity definition and/or its contents. Copyright statements are generally legal restrictions on the use and publishing of the activity definition.

elements.short: When the activity definition was approved by publisher
elements.definition: The date on which the resource content was approved by the publisher. Approval happens once when the content is officially approved for usage.

elements.short: When the activity definition was last reviewed
elements.definition: The date on which the resource content was last reviewed. Review happens periodically after approval but does not change the original approval date.

elements.short: When the activity definition is expected to be used
elements.definition: The period during which the activity definition content was or is planned to be in active use.

elements.short: E.g. Education, Treatment, Assessment, etc.
elements.definition: Descriptive topics related to the content of the activity. Topics provide a high-level categorization of the activity that can be useful for filtering and searching.

binding.description: High-level categorization of the definition, used for searching, sorting, and filtering.

elements.short: Who authored the content
elements.definition: An individiual or organization primarily involved in the creation and maintenance of the content.

elements.short: Who edited the content
elements.definition: An individual or organization primarily responsible for internal coherence of the content.

elements.short: Who reviewed the content
elements.definition: An individual or organization primarily responsible for review of some aspect of the content.

elements.short: Who endorsed the content
elements.definition: An individual or organization responsible for officially endorsing the content for use in some setting.

elements.short: Additional documentation, citations, etc.
elements.definition: Related artifacts such as additional documentation, justification, or bibliographic references.

elements.short: Logic used by the activity definition
elements.definition: A reference to a Library resource containing any formal logic used by the activity definition.

elements.short: Kind of resource
elements.definition: A description of the kind of resource the activity definition is representing. For example, a MedicationRequest, a ServiceRequest, or a CommunicationRequest. Typically, but not always, this is a Request resource.

binding.description: The kind of activity the definition is describing.

elements.short: What profile the resource needs to conform to
elements.definition: A profile to which the target of the activity definition is expected to conform.

elements.short: Detail type of activity
elements.definition: Detailed description of the type of activity; e.g. What lab test, what procedure, what kind of encounter.

binding.description: Detailed type of the activity; e.g. CBC.

elements.short: proposal | plan | directive | order | original-order | reflex-order | filler-order | instance-order | option
elements.definition: Indicates the level of authority/intentionality associated with the activity and where the request should fit into the workflow chain.

binding.description: Codes indicating the degree of authority/intentionality associated with a request.

elements.short: routine | urgent | asap | stat
elements.definition: Indicates how quickly the activity  should be addressed with respect to other requests.

binding.description: Identifies the level of importance to be assigned to actioning the request.

elements.isModifierReason: If true this element negates the specified action. For Example,  instead of a request for a procedure, it is a request for the procedure to not occur.
elements.short: True if the activity should not be performed
elements.definition: Set this to true if the definition is to indicate that a particular activity should NOT be performed. If true, this element should be interpreted to reinforce a negative coding. For example NPO as a code with a doNotPerform of true would still indicate to NOT perform the action.

elements.short: When activity is to occur
elements.definition: The period, timing or frequency upon which the described activity is to occur.

elements.short: Where it should happen
elements.definition: Identifies the facility where the activity will occur; e.g. home, hospital, specific clinic, etc.

elements.short: Who should participate in the action

elements.definition: Identifies the quantity expected to be consumed at once (per dose, per meal, etc.).

elements.short: Detailed dosage instructions

elements.short: What part of body to perform on
elements.definition: Indicates the sites on the subject's body where the procedure should be performed (I.e. the target sites).

binding.description: A code that identifies the anatomical location.

elements.short: What specimens are required to perform this action
elements.definition: Defines specimen requirements for the action to be performed, such as required specimens for a lab test.

elements.short: What observations are required to perform this action
elements.definition: Defines observation requirements for the action to be performed, such as body weight or surface area.

elements.short: What observations must be produced by this action
elements.definition: Defines the observations that are expected to be produced by the action.
